criteria.quote: Magikarp's jump stops at seven feet—unless it ages.
criteria.revision: Replace "unless it ages" with "but one entry says a Magikarp living many years can leap a mountain" to introduce the documented contradiction without implying that aging always unlocks it.

criteria.quote: A Magikarp living many years can leap a mountain using Splash.
How can a Pokémon with a seven-foot jump limit clear a mountain?
criteria.revision: Keep the question, but frame the apparent contradiction more precisely: "How can the same Pokédex describe Magikarp as jumping no more than seven feet, then say one living many years can leap a mountain?"

criteria.quote: Some entries cap its rare jumps at seven feet.
criteria.revision: Make the progression sharper by moving directly from the documented limit to the exception: change the third scene to "Then Platinum gives one Magikarp living many years a mountain-sized exception."

criteria.quote: The same entry calls Splash useless, even after that mountain leap.

criteria.revision: Cut or repurpose the first scene so it does not repeat the second scene's seven-foot setup. Open with the mountain claim, then reveal the seven-foot descriptions as the contradiction: "A Magikarp can leap a mountain—with Splash. But other entries say its rare jumps never exceed seven feet."

criteria.quote: Seven-foot cap or mountain leap: which feels more like Magikarp?
criteria.revision: Make the ending resolve the contradiction before inviting debate: "Magikarp is described as both a rare seven-foot jumper and, after many years, a mountain leaper—and even then, Splash is still called useless."

criteria.quote: Seven-foot cap or mountain leap: which feels more like Magikarp?
criteria.revision: Make the two credible positions explicitly evidence-based: "Which description should define Magikarp: the entries calling its rare jumps no more than seven feet, or the entry saying one living many years can leap a mountain with Splash?"
